normalized.answer: Exact 2002 words 'Identifier-3, ... , identifier-n' against 2023's 'Identifier-3, … , identifier-n': only the ellipsis character differs, the requirement 'shall reference an elementary item described implicitly or explicitly as usage display or national' (§2002:14.8.21.2 SR2) is the same, and SR-14.9.22.3-2 is the right pointer.

behaviour-switch.answer: The switch (DialectBehavior.InspectBeforeFromFirstEligiblePosition) decides only where an operand's BEFORE delimiter is looked for when it also has AFTER; at 2002 the BEFORE portion runs from the leftmost position (§2002:14.8.21.3 GR8b) and the operand participates where it meets the AFTER portion (§2002:14.8.21.3 GR8). This syntax rule is decided at compile time and the switch changes only the run-time region (InspectBinder.BindPhrases into BoundInspect.BeforeFromLeftmost); it refuses nothing at any edition (VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE row 7.65), so the rule's 2002 behaviour is the evidence-2002 the read names, unchanged by the switch.
